subject: general
question: Archana can eat 21 litchis in 60 minutes. She wants to know how many minutes it would take her to eat 35 litchis at the same pace.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time taken to eat 1 litchi = 60 ÷ 21 minutes.

Time taken to eat 35 litchis = (60 ÷ 21) × 35 = 20 × 5 = 100 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 100 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of litchis eaten initially (L₁) = 21

Time taken initially (T₁) = 60 minutes

Target number of litchis (L₂) = 35

**Formula Used:**

Since the pace is constant, the ratio of litchis eaten to time taken remains constant:

L₁ ÷ T₁ = L₂ ÷ T₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4bce527e600261bd35a98386ea5a8facbd348c359feeb88572f98b25c5fb3377.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 21 ÷ 60 = 35 ÷ T₂

⇒ T₂ = (35 × 60) ÷ 21

⇒ T₂ = (5 × 60) ÷ 3

⇒ T₂ = 5 × 20

⇒ T₂ = 100 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 100 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Proportion

When two quantities are in direct proportion, an increase in one leads to a proportional increase in the other. The ratio x ÷ y remains constant throughout.

Unitary Method

A problem-solving method where we first find the value of a single unit (by dividing), and then multiply this individual value to find the required total value.</p
